correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and boundary assumptions have been checked. The positive simplex is invariant, the logistic comparison yields a positive lower bound on total biomass, and the exact nonincreasing ratios give an eventual lower bound on the top species. The resulting ecological clock diverges. An induction in the triangular rescaled ODE shows even coordinates integrable and vanishing, odd coordinates positive, for arbitrary finite n. Logistic forcing tends to zero because each predation product contains an extinct even coordinate; hence total biomass tends to 1-d/r. Normalization proves the limit and parameter invariance; the n=3 expression follows by direct integration. The p=0 limit is separately computed. The included numerical program checks concrete cases but is not treated as proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: For three or more species our dynamics admits an entire positive-odd-coordinate equilibrium simplex, and the limit varies with initial ratios; it therefore has no single equilibrium that attracts all positive initial states, so Hou’s sufficient point-attractor criteria do not dominate the claim. Invasion-cycle criteria address a distinct cyclic mechanism; this theorem concerns an acyclic feed-forward chain.

value.rationale: The motivating study characterizes admissible independent-set supports and local equilibria but does not identify which equilibrium a completely seeded homogeneous ecological chain reaches. The theorem provides global species-selection, an exactly characterized initial-abundance-dependent coexistence map, and a singular boundary at arbitrarily weak predation. Thus it is a structural dynamical result addressing a natural population-selection gap, not a cosmetic reparameterization or an arbitrary finite slice; it makes explicit ecological predictions distinguishing finite observation times from infinite-time outcomes.
